newsitem.title: CANARY ISLANDS: SOCCER-EUROPE AND AFRICA TO STRENGTHEN SOCCER TIES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EUROPE AND AFRICA TO STRENGTHEN SOCCER TIES.

text.p: Cash-rich European soccer is to provide funds to help impoverished African nations develop the game on the African continent, UEFA general secretary Gerhard Aigner said on Thursday.

Starting with January's inaugural Europe v Africa representative match in Lisbon which kicks off 1997 as the 'Year against Racism', Aigner announced a number of proposals agreed at Thursday's UEFA Executive Committee meeting.
These include an Under-17 tournament for eight countries -- four from Africa and four from Europe to be staged every two years.

He said UEFA would also sponsor a different African country's football association every two years; that European football associations would also start to sponsor African football associations and that regular representative matches between European and African teams would become a regular feature of the soccer calendar.
The first of these will be in Lisbon on January 29 when the European Select XI faces an African Select Xi. The European team will be managed by former Dutch coach Rinus Michels.
The revenue from the match will be used to launch the development of football projects in Africa.

"There is and will be a greater co-operation between UEFA and the CAF (Confederation of African Football)" said Aigner, announcing details of what will be known as the Meridian project. He said the first Under-17 tournament would start on January 31 and feature France, Greece, Portugal and Spain from Europe and Ghana, Guinea, Ivory Coast and Nigeria from Africa."
"We will select the teams to take part in the tournament on the merits of their work done by the national association in youth football," Aigner added.

UEFA and its African counterparts are due to meet in Barcelona at FIFA's Executive Committee meeting at the weekend which could prove a little embarassing, at least initially, for UEFA's president Lennart Johansson, who was quoted by a Swedish newspaper last month calling Africans "blackies."
UEFA's Executive Committee nevertheless gave their president their full backing on Thursday.

In a statement UEFA pledged its "wholehearted support for the UEFA president," adding: "The UEFA executive committee unanimously and decidedly opposed all press reports which accused Lennart Johansson of racist slander...The Committee assures the president of UEFA of its full support."
